sections.headline: Deterministic Proof
paragraphs: Most systems rely on trust: policies, screenshots, declarations, and after-the-fact audits. That approach breaks when incentives shift, when pressure hits, or when humans misremember.
Deterministic Proof means the system itself produces an enforced history. It becomes difficult—or impossible—to claim something happened without the evidence trail that proves it.
The objective is simple: reduce uncertainty by design, and make integrity the default.

sections.headline: If it matters, prove it.
sections.subheadline: Choose the Guard that matches your failure mode.

guards.name: Ledger Guard
guards.problem: Records can be altered, backfilled, or selectively presented after the fact.
guards.enforcement: Append-only ledgering with deterministic entry hashes and replayable history.

hero.headline: Ledger Guard
hero.subheadline: When the history matters, ambiguity is the enemy. Ledger Guard enforces append-only reality.

sections.problem: If the record can be rewritten, the record can be weaponised.
sections.solution: Ledger Guard enforces an append-only evidence trail. Events become provable—not persuasive.

guards.name: Logic Guard
guards.problem: Systems drift into impossible states when rules are implied, scattered, or manually enforced.
guards.enforcement: Invariant enforcement at runtime: invalid transitions are blocked before they land.

hero.headline: Logic Guard
hero.subheadline: If a system can drift into invalid state, it eventually will. Logic Guard blocks it at the gate.

sections.problem: Policy without enforcement is just a suggestion.
sections.solution: Logic Guard makes invariants executable. The system cannot proceed unless rules are satisfied.
